brief: A wall-hung spice rack: at least three bins, hung from keyhole hangers.

requirements.requirement: Spice rack with at least three bins
requirements.evidence: There are three full-depth bins with three compartments each (bin:-1,0,0, bin:0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0), nine compartments in all.
Each cell has a keyhole hanger (accessory:0#-1,0#2, accessory:0#0,0#2 and accessory:0#1,0#2), all in the same slot on the same long side, so they line up as the back face.

The keyhole hangers are where the rack hangs on screws in the wall. The configurator only checks fit, so it can't tell whether the hangers, the screws or the print material will carry the weight of full spice jars. That needs checking in real life.

finish.summary: I built a spice rack from three hex cells side by side, about 507 mm wide. Each cell holds a full-depth bin split into three compartments, so there are nine spice spots. Each cell has a keyhole hanger on the same long side, so all three line up on one back face and the rack lifts onto screws already in the wall. The open faces are capped and the joints between cells are bolted. The build check passed with no rule issues and no mesh clashes. I added no props: the catalog has no spice jars, and the kitchen props on offer (mugs, glasses, cutlery) wouldn't show what the rack is for.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762
M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
